_about: Loss and grief (dungeon/life/loss.py, v0.14 #71): funeral customs by culture and era (as world/data/wedding.json), the news a companion texts when someone close dies ({who}, {when}), small things that bring them back while grieving (completing "Today something brought {them} back: ..."; {they}/{them}/{their} are the late person's pronouns, past tense only), and an obituary's closing sentence ({name}, {their}). Grief is sadness and missing someone: nothing here reads as self-harm. Obituaries name no workplace or trade (the same line runs in every era and city) and say the name once. A culture's `never` names places no funeral is held at (a Shinto shrine in Japan).

us.service: a service with readings and a eulogy, then the burial
us.after: food back at the house afterward

uk.service: a service with hymns and a eulogy, then the committal
uk.after: the wake at a pub or the house afterward

japan.service: the wake (tsuya) the evening before, then the funeral service with incense offerings
japan.after: the cremation and a quiet meal with the family
japan.mourning: The family's memorial on the 49th day matters most.

south-korea.service: three days of mourning at the funeral hall, where guests bow and offer condolences, then the burial or cremation
south-korea.after: a meal with the family at the hall
south-korea.year: the memorial rites on the anniversary
south-korea.venue: the funeral hall at the hospital

us-1920s.service: a viewing in the parlor, then a church service and the burial
us-1920s.after: a gathering at the house with food the neighbors brought
us-1920s.mourning: The family wears black for some months.

us-1880s.service: a laying-out at home, then a church service and the burial
us-1880s.after: a meal at the house afterward
us-1880s.mourning: The family keeps to mourning black for a year.

uk-victorian.service: a procession with mutes and plumed horses, a church service and the burial
uk-victorian.after: a funeral tea at the house
uk-victorian.wear: full mourning black, crape and jet
uk-victorian.mourning: The family keeps full mourning for a year, half mourning after.

medieval-england.service: a vigil through the night, the requiem mass and the burial in the churchyard
medieval-england.after: a funeral ale and alms for the poor
medieval-england.mourning: Masses are said for them at the month's mind.

modern.service: a service with a eulogy, then the burial or cremation
modern.after: a gathering afterward to share stories

industrial.service: a service at the chapel and the burial
industrial.after: tea and sandwiches at the house afterward
industrial.wear: black or the darkest clothes they own

old.service: a vigil, the rites and the burial
old.after: a funeral feast in their memory
